blocks.html:
Worth knowing: the old flow is still running

As of this read, Post-Purchase Onboarding (RETIRING) is still live with 13 emails switched on, and it still triggers on Placed Order. That means a customer who orders today enters the old journey as well as the new one, and several of the emails are the same. Until it is switched off, the old line on the chart below is not a tail, it is a live second journey.

This note writes itself out of the report on the next run after the old flow's emails are set to draft.

What changed

Until 5 October, one flow handled everything after a purchase. It started the moment the order was placed, so every email after that was counted off a clock that had nothing to do with where the parcel actually was. A customer waiting three weeks on a pre-order got the same sequence, on the same timing, as a customer whose parcel arrived on Tuesday.

That flow has been replaced by three, each tied to something that really happened:

  • Pre-Order: The Wait fires when a pre-order is placed, and keeps people warm until the stock lands.
  • Onboarding fires when the order is fulfilled, so the sequence starts when the parcel is genuinely on its way.
  • Delivered fires when the courier marks the parcel delivered, which is the only honest moment to ask someone how they like it.

This report watches the handover. It is deliberately a transition report, not a performance report: for the first few weeks the numbers below are mostly a picture of timing, not of copy.

blocks.html:
Expect a gap, not a cliff

The old flow sent within minutes of an order. The new Onboarding flow waits for fulfilment, and Delivered waits for the courier. So volume does not move across on the day: it arrives a few days later, as the orders placed around the switch work their way through dispatch. A dip in the week of the cutover is the design working, not a fault.

blocks.title: Old journey vs new journey

blocks.html:
The clock moved. The old flow measured from the order. The new ones measure from dispatch and delivery. "Day 14" is a different moment in each, so do not line the two sequences up email by email.

The creative mostly did not change. Eleven of the new Onboarding emails are the same emails, moved across. If open rate moves, the first suspect is timing and audience, not the writing.

Pre-orders are a different population. They were a small share of orders over the last month, so the Pre-Order flow will always look small next to the others. Small is correct. It is not underperforming.

The old flow was retired, not deleted. Its emails stay in the account so the history stays readable. The long tail of zeros on its line is the point.

Two flows are excluded. A part-shipment variant and a split-orders variant were built but never switched on. They are left out of every number here.
